documented_impact: Water/pasture depletion, livestock stress and earlier/farther pastoral mobility.
fcv_mediator: Access rules for water, grazing land and migration routes; land/resource governance; pre-existing grievances.
possible_consequence: Where governance and dispute-resolution institutions are weak or contested, increased concentrations of livestock and altered mobility may intensify local resource disputes or pre-existing tensions.
geographies: Current pastoral evidence is strongest in central/northern Somalia
conflict-pathway evidence is specifically documented in Hirshabelle/Galmudug NLA
affected_groups: farmers and communities along migration routes
uncertainty: No national evidence establishes a fixed drought -> conflict relationship; the best direct pathway study is geographically restricted.
resilience_factors: clear access arrangements and credible local dispute-resolution mechanisms
compact_statement: Drought-driven livelihood and mobility changes can raise local resource pressures, but whether these become conflict depends on governance, historical relations and institutions.

climate_pressure: Failed Deyr rains and continuing drought.
documented_impact: Severely reduced Deyr crop output and livestock productivity.
fcv_mediator: Food markets, purchasing power, conflict disruption, currency conditions and humanitarian assistance.
possible_consequence: Combined production and market shocks may deepen food insecurity, distress coping and displacement, increasing vulnerability in already fragile communities.
geographies: with particularly severe conditions in specified livelihood zones and districts
uncertainty: IPC classifications integrate multiple drivers and do not assign an independent causal percentage to climate.
compact_statement: 2026 food insecurity reflects climate-linked production stress interacting with conflict, markets, disease, services and humanitarian financing.

fcv_mediator: Settlement access, urban service capacity, land/property access, livelihoods and host-IDP relations.
possible_consequence: Large displacement flows may increase demand for water, housing, livelihoods and municipal services and can aggravate vulnerability or grievances where delivery and land governance are weak.
geographies: urban implications should be assessed city by city
alternative_explanations: poverty and established patterns of urbanization
uncertainty: UNHCR reports conflict and drought jointly; it does not allocate the “nearly 90%” figure between them or establish the downstream grievance pathway. (UNHCR Data Portal)
compact_statement: Drought and conflict jointly drive displacement; resulting FCV effects depend on urban/service and land-governance capacity.

documented_impact: Need for climate planning and local delivery.
fcv_mediator: Insecurity, territorial access, institutional fragility and operating costs.
possible_consequence: Insecure or inaccessible areas may receive less consistent adaptation programming, monitoring and service delivery, producing geographically unequal resilience.
geographies: national relevance plausible but magnitude unquantified
affected_groups: Communities in insecure or hard-to-access areas
uncertainty: The observed UNDP programme-design choice cannot quantify all adaptation excluded by insecurity. (UNDP Climate Change Adaptation)
compact_statement: Insecurity can directly narrow where adaptation programmes operate, making FCV an obstacle to climate resilience.

documented_impact: Recurring demand for water, social protection, food-security and recovery services.
fcv_mediator: Limited fiscal space, contested federal arrangements, institutional capacity and absorptive constraints.
possible_consequence: Rapidly expanding crisis/resilience portfolios may overload systems or become fiscally unsustainable even when individual projects deliver useful outputs.
uncertainty: IEG evidence is specific to the World Bank portfolio rather than all adaptation financing.
resilience_factors: stronger coordination and realistic absorptive-capacity assessment
compact_statement: Institutional and fiscal fragility can make climate-resilience gains difficult to sustain even where projects work.

fcv_mediator: Information flows, anticipatory financing, government/humanitarian coordination and community resource management.
possible_consequence: Earlier and better-coordinated response could protect livelihoods and services and thereby reduce some pressures that otherwise feed displacement or grievance; conflict-prevention effects are not independently demonstrated.
uncertainty: Early-warning use and preparedness activation are documented more strongly than avoided losses or conflict effects.
resilience_factors: scalable safety nets and coordinated crisis governance
compact_statement: Somalia has meaningful anticipatory and community resilience capacities, but their effect on FCV outcomes remains under-evaluated.
